# Changelog

<!-- Generated by pnpm changelog:generate from src/content/releases.ts. Do not edit manually. -->

User-visible changes for [stugx.CASL](https://github.com/LMstugx/stugx-casl). The application also packages the same registry for offline EN, JA, and zh-CN viewing.

## 1.0.0 - 2026-11-09 (Stable)

The interface is rebuilt as one workbench around a redrawn COMET II datapath. The C++ core and its behaviour are unchanged.

[Open the public Web application](https://stugx-casl.pages.dev/)

### Added

- One workbench frame for every view: tool bar, source pane, datapath with the data beside it, output dock, and control bar. The page no longer scrolls; each region scrolls on its own.
- A redrawn datapath with real component shapes. Buses are always drawn, a path gets colour and an arrowhead only while the current step uses it, and a rewritten value keeps its previous value beside it.
- Step animation: after a forward step the control signal, the value travelling along its path, and a pulse where it lands play once. Reverse steps play nothing, and nothing moves when the system asks for reduced motion.
- Breakpoints and Run to breakpoint. Click a line number, or press F9 in the editor. Breakpoints belong to the page session and are never stored.
- Global shortcuts: Space to step, Shift+Space to reverse one instruction, F5 to run, F6 to stop, Ctrl+Enter to assemble, Ctrl+S to save. They never act inside the editor, a text field, or a dialog.
- The output dock can be collapsed, and it opens the Console and focuses its field when the program waits for input.

### Improved

- The source editor, its errors, and the project modules stay on screen in every view. The source pane can be hidden without losing the editor's text or undo history.
- The datapath says in words what the run state means: not assembled, stale after an edit, waiting for input, finished, or stopped by an error. After a finished run the editor names the line that ran last.
- In COMET Mode the phase track and the current phase sit directly under the datapath instead of above it.
- Layouts for 1180, 1280, 1440 and 1920 pixel windows in English, Japanese and Simplified Chinese: no page overflow, a single-row tool bar, and a datapath that is never narrower than 600 pixels.

### Fixed

- The debugger edit dialog no longer shows the previous target's draft for one frame. Opening FR right after editing SP could show OF as already checked.

### Known Issues

- In CASL Mode on a window less than about 800 pixels high, the lower part of the datapath is reached by scrolling its column. Hiding the source pane or collapsing the dock makes room for it.
- Windows narrower than 1180 pixels are not supported and scroll horizontally, as before.

## 0.1.0 - 2026-07-17 (Preview)

The learning studio is available as a production WASM application on Cloudflare Pages, with the same release registry packaged for offline desktop use.

[Open the public Web application](https://stugx-casl.pages.dev/)

### Added

- A public Cloudflare Pages entry point with production WASM, security headers, cache rules, and remote smoke coverage.
- New, Open, Save, Save As, Dirty guards, and revision-derived beforeunload behavior for one working document.
- Independent safe persistence for locale, UI preferences, the last built-in example, and built-in lesson progress.
- An offline Tauri Windows demonstration build that reuses the React, Vite, Monaco, and WASM frontend without adding native filesystem permissions.
- A structured, multilingual Changelog generated from the same offline release registry used by the application.
- Binary64 double storage observation with four high-word-first COMET II words, runtime literal stores, four-word copy assignment, and a live Double Value Inspector.
- CASL Mode covers all 28 official COMET II machine instructions, IN / OUT / RPUSH / RPOP macro expansion, WaitingInput, and symbol and literal tables.
- Debugger controls edit GR0-GR7, PR, SP, the three COMET II flags, individual memory words, and runtime machine words, with Full Clear and epoch-based mutation ownership.
- COMET Mode executes real Fetch, Decode, Effective Address, Operand Read, Execute, Write Back, Flag Update, and Instruction Complete microcycles across all 28 machine instructions.
- COMET Mode can reverse one committed microcycle within the current history epoch through the same C++ Core, Mock, and WASM contract, with a bounded history of 1,000 entries.
- Reverse Instruction atomically restores the latest real machine instruction, including partial microcycles, Memory, Registers, OF / SF / ZF, Trace, Source Mapping, Machine highlighting, and Circuit state. Macro source lines reverse one expanded machine instruction at a time.
- The deterministic Multi-program Linker assembles independent CASL modules, selects an explicit main module, exports START program labels, applies auditable address relocations, and executes cross-module CALL / RET in one linked COMET II image.

### Improved

- EN, JA, and zh-CN presentation for application controls and structured diagnostics, while technical identities remain locale-independent.
- The teacher-feedback-driven Unified Observation Workspace keeps the live Circuit visible while Registers, Memory, Stack, Code / Machine, Source Mapping, Trace, Console, or Inspector data is selected. CASL / COMET execution mode is independent from observation data.
- Show Both, Focus Circuit, Focus Data, and session-only Follow Execution coordinate Circuit and data highlighting. The 1180 / 1280 layouts stack the panes safely, while 1440 / 1920 use readable side-by-side panes.
- The WCASL-compatible workflow offers hexadecimal, signed decimal, unsigned decimal, and binary displays plus explicit assembled, zero-DS, and FFFF-DS reload modes.
- The COMET II flag register is modeled as the official OF, SF, and ZF bits only; shift instructions write the shifted-out bit to OF and no CF is exposed.
- Source, machine word, microcycle trace, and clean active circuit flow stay aligned through stugx.CASL Teaching Microarchitecture v1, an explanatory model rather than a claim about a unique physical implementation.
- Reverse Microstep atomically restores VM state, Trace, Source Mapping, Machine Code highlighting, and Circuit flow, while refusing to cross debugger mutation, Reset, Reload, Full Clear, SVC, or input/output boundaries.
- Project and Module identities, relocation and placement tables, module-aware Machine Code / Trace / Source Mapping, and hard relink history barriers keep linked execution auditable without changing single-file behavior.

### Security

- Production builds require the WASM backend, omit public source maps, and never silently substitute the Mock backend.

### Known Issues

- The C++ path is a teaching subset, not a complete C++ compiler; arrays, pointers, classes, templates, recursion, and the full standard library are outside the current scope.
- The Windows demo is unsigned and still uses the browser file adapter boundary; native Tauri file dialogs and updates are deferred.
- Double support is limited to local storage, finite literals, and copy assignment; arithmetic, comparison, conversion, parameters, returns, and arrays remain unsupported.
- Reverse history is limited to the current history epoch and 1,000 retained microcycles. Redo, Reverse Run, Reverse Macro, cross-SVC, cross-I/O, mutation, Reload, Reset, or Full Clear rollback, and a complete time-travel debugger are not supported.
- The linker does not read a proprietary WCASL project format, persist project sessions, scan directories, perform dynamic linking, accept C/C++ object files, or concatenate source files.

Release references: [Commit](https://github.com/LMstugx/stugx-casl/commit/de1b28d6440f9a791772488443cb03d4703b73a9)
